notes: GPUI PANEL. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React. You have no training knowledge of this exact API, so read before writing: rever/src/main.rs (the app shell: how views, listeners, hover, scrolling, text fields and theme are used here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src (theme tokens, icons, strings via `Lang::t`, the TextInput entity, preview::run), vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs (uniform_list.rs, scrollable.rs, input.rs) and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs for exact method names. What to build: a view struct implementing gpui::Render that reproduces the React component's layout, sizes, colors and behaviors (connection list, frame list with direction and opcode, filters, the payload composer and send button, the live indicator). Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css tokens (in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; if a token is missing, define it locally and list it in your report). Data: WebSocket requests and frames live in rever_core::traffic::TrafficStore (read rever-core/src/traffic.rs); the view takes `Arc<Mutex<TrafficStore>>` and a `refresh` method. Sending a frame goes through IPC in the React code: take that as a trait object or boxed closure argument (connection id and payload in, a result out) so the host can supply it later; the preview supplies a fake. The file imports lib/ws-sequence.ts, which someone else is porting into another crate right now: port the small part you need inside this crate and say so in a comment. All user-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the same keys the TSX uses. Keep logic in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; the .tsx gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-websocket --example preview_websocket` shows the view with realistic fixture data (use rever_ui_kit::preview::run). Look at your own work: while it runs, `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_websocket /tmp/preview_websocket.png` captures only that window; read the PNG, compare with what the TSX would render, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, and do not run the `rever` app. The first build of a GPUI crate takes a few minutes.
